stem: Early humans defined a day using which repeating natural event?
options: The rising and setting of the Sun
explanation: Correct option: (C). The chapter states that a day was defined by the cycle of rising and setting of the Sun. The phases of the Moon and the seasons also repeat, but over much longer intervals (about a month and a year), so they do not define a day. River floods are not a regular daily event.

stem: The bowl of a Ghatika-yantra took 24 minutes to fill and sink, and this interval was called one ghati. How many ghatis made up a 24-hour day?
explanation: Correct option: (C). A day has 24 h = 24 x 60 min = 1440 min. Number of ghatis = 1440 min / 24 min = 60. The value 24 confuses ghatis with hours; 40 and 100 come from wrong division.

stem: Water clocks in which water flowed out of a marked vessel were not very accurate. What was the main reason?
options: Water evaporated faster at night than by day
The flow slowed down as the water level dropped
The vessel markings faded with daily use

stem: A pendulum bob starts at the mean position O. A and B are its two extreme positions. Which movement of the bob is exactly one oscillation?
options: O to A and then back to O
A to B, without coming back
O to A, then to B, then back to O
A to O, without going further
explanation: Correct option: (C). One oscillation starting from O is O to A, A to B and B back to O, so the bob returns to its starting point moving the same way. O to A and back covers only half the path; A to B is half an oscillation; A to O is a quarter.

stem: Pendulum P has a 100 cm thread and a 50 g bob, Q has a 100 cm thread and a 200 g bob, and R has a 50 cm thread and a 50 g bob. All are at the same place. Which statement is correct?
options: P and Q have the same time period, but R's differs
P and R have the same time period, but Q's differs
All three have different time periods
All three have the same time period
explanation: Correct option: (A). At a given place the time period of a simple pendulum depends on its length, not on the bob's mass. P and Q have the same length, so they have the same time period even though Q's bob is heavier; R is shorter, so its time period is different. P and R share the bob's mass but not the length, so they do not match.

stem: In a 100 m race all runners start together. After 8 s, which runner is running the fastest?
options: The one who has taken the most steps
The one who is running in the inner lane

explanation: Correct option: (A). Distance = 1.8 km = 1.8 x 1000 m = 1800 m; time = 10 min = 10 x 60 s = 600 s. Speed = 1800 m / 600 s = 3 m/s. 0.18 m/s divides 1.8 by 10 without converting; 180 m/s converts only the distance (1800 m / 10); 18 m/s wrongly divides 1800 m by 100 s.

stem: A cheetah runs at 30 m/s and a car moves at 90 km/h. Which statement is correct?
options: The car is faster by 60 km/h
Both move at the same speed
The car is faster by 5 m/s
The cheetah is faster by 5 m/s

stem: An object is said to be in uniform linear motion when it moves
options: along a circular path at a constant speed
along a straight line with changing speed
back and forth about a fixed point
along a straight line at a constant speed
explanation: Correct option: (D). Uniform linear motion is motion along a straight line with a constant speed. Motion along a circle is not linear, a changing speed along a straight line is non-uniform linear motion, and back-and-forth motion about a point is oscillatory.

stem: Which of these is an example of non-uniform linear motion?
options: A car on an empty straight highway at a steady 80 km/h
A car on a straight city road in heavy traffic
The bob of a pendulum swinging to and fro
A train between two points at a fixed speed
explanation: Correct option: (B). In heavy traffic a car on a straight road keeps speeding up and slowing down, so its speed changes while it moves in a line: non-uniform linear motion. stem: A scooter on a straight road covers 100 m in each of the first three 10 s intervals and 60 m in the fourth 10 s interval. Which statement is correct?
options: Uniform over the whole 40 s of its motion
Non-uniform for the first 30 s, uniform after
Non-uniform throughout, as it never kept pace
Uniform for the first 30 s, non-uniform over all 40 s
explanation: Correct option: (D). In the first 30 s it covers equal distances (100 m) in equal intervals, so that part is uniform. In the fourth interval it covers only 60 m, so over the full 40 s it covers unequal distances in equal intervals and the motion is non-uniform. The other options misread where the distances change.

stem: Using the data in the case, which conclusion is correct?
options: Q is uniform; both have an average speed of 72 km/h
P is uniform; both have an average speed of 72 km/h
P is uniform; Q has the higher average speed
Both are uniform; each moves at 1.2 km/min
explanation: Correct option: (B). Car P covers 1.2 km in every minute (0, 1.2, 2.4, 3.6, 4.8, 6.0 km), so it is in uniform linear motion. Car Q covers 0.8, 1.2, 1.0, 1.6 and 1.4 km in successive minutes, so it is non-uniform. Both cover 6.0 km in 5 min: average speed = 6.0 km / 5 min = 1.2 km/min = 1.2 x 60 km/h = 72 km/h for each. So Q is not uniform, Q's average speed is not higher, and only P moves at a steady 1.2 km/min.
